privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.subtitle: AppWatch tracks how apps perform on the App Store, straight from your device. This policy explains, plainly, what it stores, what it sends, and to whom.

body: AppWatch is an App Store tracking app for developers and app enthusiasts, made by NoSky Studios Ltd. It follows apps' chart positions, ratings, reviews, and prices, and — if you link your own App Store Connect account — your sales, proceeds, and analytics.

AppWatch has no server. We do not have accounts, we do not ask you to sign in, and we do not run analytics, advertising, or tracking of any kind. Everything AppWatch fetches goes directly between your device and Apple (plus a few exchange-rate services), and everything it keeps is stored on your device. None of it is sent to us.
The rest of this policy explains exactly what is stored, what is sent, and how to delete it.
AppWatch is published by NoSky Studios Ltd (RC 7631695), a company registered in Nigeria ("NoSky Studios", "we", "us", or "our").
This Privacy Policy applies to the AppWatch app for iPhone and iPad. For any privacy question, contact us at [privacy@noskystudios.ng](mailto:privacy@noskystudios.ng).
We want to be specific, because "we value your privacy" means little on its own. In AppWatch there is:
list: No server and no account. AppWatch does not send anything to a server operated by us. You do not create a profile, and we never ask for your name, email, or phone number.

No analytics or usage tracking. AppWatch contains no analytics, crash-reporting, advertising, or attribution software, and no third-party code libraries of any kind. We do not measure how you use the app.
No advertising identifiers. AppWatch does not request the App Tracking Transparency permission and does not access the device advertising identifier (IDFA).
No access to your App Store Connect data. Your sales, proceeds, analytics, and reviews travel only between your device and Apple. We never see them.
No selling or sharing of data. We do not sell, rent, or share your personal information, because we do not receive it in the first place.

body: Everything AppWatch keeps is stored locally on your device, in storage private to the app. This includes:
list: The apps you watch and their public App Store details — name, developer, icon, price, genre, version, description, screenshots, and similar.
Chart history: each app's rank by country, chart, and category over time, its best positions, and the checks AppWatch has run.

Ratings, reviews, and prices: daily rating, review, price, and version history, plus cached copies of public App Store reviews. Public reviews include the reviewer's chosen nickname and country, exactly as Apple publishes them.
Your alert rules and alert history, and your settings — such as your home country (which starts from your device's region), currency, and appearance.

If you link App Store Connect: the account's name, Key ID, and Vendor Number, the list of apps on the account, and the sales, proceeds, and analytics reports AppWatch downloads from Apple. These reports contain aggregated figures by country and date — not your customers' names or contact details.
after: AppWatch does not use iCloud sync for this data, and there is no cloud copy of your library. Your watched apps, history, and settings are included in your normal device backups that you control through Apple; App Store Connect reports are excluded from device backups and are downloaded again from Apple when needed.

sections.h: Your App Store Connect API key
body: Linking App Store Connect is optional. If you do, you give AppWatch an App Store Connect API key that you create in your own App Store Connect account: its Issuer ID, Key ID, private key (.p8), and your Vendor Number.

The private key is stored in your iCloud Keychain, Apple's end-to-end encrypted password store, so that it is available on your other devices signed in to the same Apple Account. It is not stored on any NoSky Studios server, and we cannot see or access it.

The private key never leaves your devices except through iCloud Keychain. AppWatch uses it on your device to sign a short-lived access token, and sends only that token to Apple's App Store Connect API (api.appstoreconnect.apple.com). No one else receives it.

You can unlink an account at any time in Settings. Unlinking deletes the key from iCloud Keychain on all your devices, along with that account's downloaded reports. You can also revoke the key at any time in App Store Connect.

sections.h: Things AppWatch does in your App Store Connect account
body: With a linked key, AppWatch reads your sales reports, the apps on your account, customer reviews, and analytics reports. It also takes two kinds of action on your behalf, only when you use the related feature:
list: Replying to reviews. If you write a reply to a customer review, AppWatch sends it to Apple, which publishes it publicly on the App Store next to that review. You can delete a reply from AppWatch, which asks Apple to remove it.

Analytics reports. To show App Store analytics, AppWatch asks App Store Connect to start generating ongoing analytics reports for your apps. That request is created in your App Store Connect account and is managed by Apple.

body: AppWatch makes network requests only to the services below, and only to power its features. Here is the complete list:
list: Apple's public App Store services. To check charts, look up and search apps, and read ratings, reviews, and prices, AppWatch contacts Apple's public App Store services (such as rss.marketingtools.apple.com, itunes.apple.com, and apps.apple.com). Requests contain app IDs, country codes, your search terms, and a language setting — nothing about you. App icons and screenshots are downloaded from Apple's servers.
Apple's App Store Connect API. Only if you link an account, as described above.

Exchange rates. To show prices and proceeds in your currency, AppWatch fetches reference exchange rates from ExchangeRate-API (open.er-api.com), with Fawaz Ahmed's currency API (via cdn.jsdelivr.net) and Frankfurter (api.frankfurter.dev) as fallbacks. These requests contain no information about you or your apps.

Apple system features. AppWatch can show App Store pages inside the app, and can translate reviews using Apple's Translation feature. Purchases go through Apple's App Store. These are provided and handled by Apple.
after: These providers receive only the information described above, and their use of it is governed by their own privacy policies: [Apple's Privacy Policy](https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/), [ExchangeRate-API](https://www.exchangerate-api.com/terms), [jsDelivr](https://www.jsdelivr.com/terms/privacy-policy-jsdelivr-net), and [Frankfurter](https://frankfurter.dev). As with any internet request, these providers may receive your device's IP address and standard request information; we do not receive that information and do not combine it with anything about you.

body: AppWatch is free to use with one watched app. AppWatch Pro — a one-time App Store purchase, not a subscription — lets you watch as many apps as you like. All purchases are handled by Apple through the App Store using your Apple Account.

Payment is processed entirely by Apple. AppWatch never sees or receives your card, bank, or payment details. To manage your purchase, the app receives from Apple only the fact that a valid purchase exists — not your identity or payment information. Purchases, restores, and refunds are governed by Apple's terms and [Apple's Privacy Policy](https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/).

The only permission AppWatch asks for is notifications, and only if you turn on alerts. Its notifications are local notifications, generated on your device — for example when an app moves in the charts, gets a new rating or review, changes price, or releases a new version, a summary of yesterday's downloads and proceeds, or a reminder that a full check is due. AppWatch does not use push notifications and does not register your device with any messaging server.
Notifications can show business figures, such as proceeds, on your Lock Screen. You can turn individual alerts off in AppWatch, or hide notification previews in the iOS Settings app.

AppWatch uses iOS background refresh to run chart checks while you are not using it, and may keep the screen awake while a check you started is running. AppWatch does not request location, contacts, camera, microphone, photos, or tracking permissions.
You can export rankings, history, ratings, prices, and sales as CSV files, and share images of an app's chart positions, using the iOS share sheet. What you share, and with whom, is up to you.

"Back Up to Files" creates a single backup file containing your watched apps, history, settings, cached App Store data, and any downloaded App Store Connect reports. Your API keys are never included. The backup file is not encrypted, so store it somewhere you trust — anyone who has the file can read your sales figures from it.

AppWatch is a business tool for app developers and is not directed to children. We do not knowingly collect personal information from anyone, including children under the age of 13 (or the equivalent minimum age in your country). Because AppWatch has no accounts and sends nothing to us, there is no such information for us to hold or delete.

Your AppWatch data is stored on your device and is protected by the security of iOS, including the device passcode, encryption, and app sandboxing that Apple provides. Your App Store Connect private key is kept in iCloud Keychain, which Apple encrypts end to end, and access tokens are signed on your device and expire within minutes.

Because your data does not sit on our servers, the most important protection is the one you control: keep your devices locked with a passcode or biometrics, keep iOS up to date, give App Store Connect keys only the access they need, and revoke any key you no longer use. No method of storage or transmission is completely secure, but keeping your data on-device removes the large, central target that a cloud database would present.

You decide how long your data is kept, because you hold it. In Settings you can stop watching any app, delete ranking history, clear the chart cache, unlink an App Store Connect account, or "Erase All Data". Erase All Data removes everything AppWatch stores on the device but keeps your linked API keys; unlink each account to remove its key too.

Deleting the AppWatch app removes its data from that device. Because API keys are kept in iCloud Keychain, unlink your accounts in AppWatch before deleting it if you want the keys removed from all your devices — and revoke the key in App Store Connect to disable it completely. If you made backup or export files, delete them wherever you saved them.

Replies you posted to customer reviews are published by Apple on the App Store; remove them from AppWatch or App Store Connect. We hold no copy of your data, so there is nothing for you to request from us and nothing for us to delete on your behalf.

Depending on where you live, data-protection laws — such as the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, the EU and UK General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), and the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA/CPRA) — give you rights over your personal information, including the rights to access, correct, delete, and port it, and to object to certain processing.

AppWatch is designed so that you already have these rights directly: your information is on your device, where you can view, export, and delete it yourself, at any time, without asking us. We do not collect, store, sell, or share your personal information, and we do not "sell" or "share" it for advertising as those terms are defined under the CCPA.

If you believe we hold personal information about you, or you have a question about your rights, contact us at [privacy@noskystudios.ng](mailto:privacy@noskystudios.ng) and we will respond. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with your local data-protection authority.

AppWatch is available worldwide, and your data stays on your device wherever you are. Requests to Apple and to the exchange-rate services are handled by those providers, which may process them on servers in another country. Those requests contain only the limited information described in the "Network connections" section above.

We may update this Privacy Policy as AppWatch evolves or as the law requires. If we ever add a feature that sends any data to a server operated by us, it will be optional and off by default, and we will update this policy before it is released. When we update the policy, we will change the "Effective" date at the top of this page and, for significant changes, note them in the app or its release notes. The current version always lives at this address. Continuing to use AppWatch after an update means you accept the revised policy.

For any question about this policy or your privacy, reach us at [privacy@noskystudios.ng](mailto:privacy@noskystudios.ng). For general help with the app, contact [appstore@noskystudios.ng](mailto:appstore@noskystudios.ng).
NoSky Studios Ltd (RC 7631695), Nigeria.
